vision.title: Counting people sounds easy. Not counting them twice doesn't.
vision.body: In a real project, YOLOv8 detects and ByteTrack follows each person across frames. A count only happens when the trajectory crosses the line — with a dead zone and cooldown so nobody is counted again.

faq.q: How much does a system cost?
faq.a: It depends on scope. After our first call I send a fixed proposal with a defined timeline and price.

faq.q: Do I need everything figured out before we talk?
faq.a: No. You only need to know the problem you want to solve — we design the scope together.

faq.q: Who owns the code and the data?
faq.a: You do. Code, database and credentials are handed over at the end of the project.

faq.q: Do you offer support after delivery?
faq.a: Yes. Adjustments and new features can be on demand or through a monthly plan.

faq.q: Do you work with clients outside Brazil?
faq.a: Yes. The whole process works remotely, with video calls, in English or Portuguese.

about.title: About
story: I'm a fullstack developer from Toledo, in southern Brazil, with a degree in Science and Technology. I got into this out of curiosity about how things work and stayed for the satisfaction of seeing a system solve a real problem.

Today I work as an RPA developer at Sicredi, automating processes with Python and PHP. On the side, I build systems for clients: a gym management SaaS running in production, business websites and computer vision projects.
Away from code, I'm a drummer, I teach drums and I play at church. Faith and family are what drive me — and they're where my wish to do good work comes from, even when nobody's watching.

how.title: Pragmatic decisions
how.body: I pick tools for the problem, not for the hype. Sometimes that's Firestore; sometimes it's PostgreSQL with Redis.

how.title: Complete delivery
how.body: Code, tests, deployment, docs and training. A system that only runs on my machine isn't delivered.

how.title: Docs for every audience
how.body: A README for developers, a manual for users and a summary for decision makers.

how.title: Local and cheap when it makes sense
how.body: The church people counter runs on a local computer with zero cloud cost. Not everything needs a paid server.
